searched: I read the Southwest Power Pool active generator interconnection list (1017 rows) and listed every Kansas gas and thermal entry.

I read the August 2026 EIA-860M table for Kansas. Every operating gas plant over 50 MW is in GEM. The planned gas entries are Viola, McNew and two 13.5 MW Riverton units. Canceled entries are Osawatomie units 2 to 8 and Nearman Creek unit 5.

I read the Kansas Register notice of April 23, 2026 for the Evergy Crooked Creek Energy Center air permit. It gives no capacity. I could not open the draft permit on the state health department's public notices page.

I read the 2025 and 2026 Evergy plan updates, the Missouri Metro 2026 plan, the Missouri Metro 2025 update and Missouri testimony of August 31, 2026. The plan charts were read from file text. I could not read anything after 2035 in the Kansas Central 2026 chart.
I did not reach the Kansas Corporation Commission filing system or the Kansas Central 2025 plan itself. I relied on a trade press report for the August 31, 2026 filing.
I searched for new plans by Sunflower, Midwest Energy, Kansas Power Pool, Empire, and the Kansas Municipal Energy Agency and found no announcement. Sunflower's 2026 filing is for a transmission line.

I searched for Kansas data centers with on-site gas and found none. Beale Infrastructure and Digital Realty have grid service agreements with Evergy. An offer to buy the closed Quindaro site for a data center is not gas generation.
The permit harvest folder for Kansas did not exist when I ran, so I did not use it.

I read the Board of Public Utilities 2024 plan in full from the corrected link the user gave. It commits to no gas. Only two study cases add gas: a 237 MW combustion turbine in 2039 if Nearman Creek 1 is retired, and replacement capacity if the two Quindaro oil turbines retire early in 2028. Neither is in the recommended action plan.

I recovered the Crooked Creek, Viola and McNew draft permits and applications from archived copies, because the department's live links return an error. I read the Kansas Corporation Commission petition for Viola and McNew through the commission's new filing site.

On October 23, 2026 I reran the search under the lower add bar. I re-read the Southwest Power Pool active list and added or answered every Kansas gas, oil and thermal request: Labette County, Quindaro diesel, McPherson, Leavenworth, Jeffrey, Sherlock, Clifton, Riverton, Walnut and the two Evergy combined cycle blocks.

I checked the new October 2026 export. It already holds Crooked Creek Energy Center, a second Clifton unit and the Sherlock Generation Project, so none of them is a new plant. The first Crooked Creek placeholder is gone from the export, so its question above is out of date.

I read the Kansas Corporation Commission petition of September 1, 2026, docket 27-EKCE-0149-PRE, through the commission's filing site, and confirmed it covers Buchanan Bluffs in Missouri and no Kansas gas plant. I also looked at the McPherson Board of Public Utilities dockets and docket 27-SEPE-0077-CON and found no new generation.

I read the 2024 EIA-860 annual proposed generator table for Kansas, the Sunflower, Midwest Energy and Kansas Municipal Energy Agency news pages and the Evergy newsroom. They list nothing new. The Evergy newsroom item of May 12, 2026 is construction at the Sumner County plant that GEM already tracks as Viola.

The Kansas Power Pool website did not answer from here. A web search and the grid list found nothing new for it beyond Walnut Energy Center, which GEM already has, and request GEN-2020-003 at Winfield that matches it.

irp_summary.Evergy Kansas Central: The 2026 update adds 355 MW of gas in 2029 (Viola), 355 MW in 2030 (McNew) and 710 MW in 2031 (Buchanan Bluffs Unit 1 in Missouri), and no gas through 2035; placeholders 2 to 5 are not in it, and I staged questions on all five and a watch item for Buchanan Bluffs.
irp_summary.Evergy Metro: The 2026 update adds 440 MW in 2031 (Mullin Creek 2 in Missouri, already in GEM under Missouri), a 355 MW half of a combined cycle in 2032 (Buchanan Bluffs Unit 2 in Missouri) and 440 MW in 2034 or 2035; nothing is new to Kansas and I staged a watch item for Buchanan Bluffs only.
irp_summary.Kansas City Board of Public Utilities: The 2024 plan commits to no new gas and says no new generation is needed in the next five years. qa.recommendation: No edit. Baird decided on October 23, 2026 that the three 33 MW turbines are one 99 MW unit, as GEM has it now, because together they pass the 50 MW bar on one grid connection.
qa.note: Unit 2 at Clifton is in GEM as one 99 MW unit made of three 33 MW Solar Turbines Titan 350 turbines, in pre-construction, starting in 2028, replacing unit 1, a Westinghouse 501 turbine from 1974. Sunflower Electric's fact sheet of July 2026 at https://sunflower-epc.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/260708_GEN_CliftonFactSheet_QFT_cf_jw_cf.pdf says it plans three 33 MW Titan 350 turbine generators, with construction beginning in September 2026 and commercial operation in summer 2028. A news report at https://www.ncktoday.com/local/sunflower-electric-power-corp-shares-details-clifton-power-plant-replacement-project repeats those facts. The Southwest Power Pool list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows one request, GEN-2026-GR1, a replacement of 97.844 MW at the Clifton substation owned by Sunflower, with cessation of the old unit on 2/15/2028, commercial operation 6/1/2028, a special study status and a request received on 9/9/2026. The three turbines together are above the bar, so one 99 MW set fits. A standard gas turbine is normally one unit each, and 33 MW is under the bar. The reviewer should pick the arrangement. The grid list figure of 97.844 MW is close to the 99 MW total.

monitor.monitor_reason: Two Evergy combined cycle blocks planned near Frazier in Buchanan County, Missouri, which is a Missouri project and belongs in a Missouri batch.
monitor.note: On September 1, 2026 Evergy Kansas Central asked the Kansas Corporation Commission for prior approval of Buchanan Bluffs Energy Center Unit 1, in docket 27-EKCE-0149-PRE. I read the petition on the commission's filing site. It describes one advanced class combined cycle gas plant of 710 MW, to be built near the city of Frazier in Buchanan County, Missouri, owned entirely by Evergy Kansas Central, with commercial operation targeted for 2031. It also says a sister plant, Unit 2, will be built in the same county and owned jointly by Evergy Missouri Metro and Evergy Missouri West. That petition page needs a script to load, so the link cannot be checked by the verifier and is not cited here. A press report at https://okenergytoday.com/2026/09/evergy-wants-more-power-plants-in-kansas-and-missouri/ covers the same filing. Missouri commission filings at https://efis.psc.mo.gov/Document/Display/888870 cover the Evergy Missouri side. Evergy's 2026 plan updates at https://investors.evergy.com/2026IRPUpdate and https://investors.evergy.com/2025IRPUpdate show the 710 MW Kansas Central block in 2031 and the Metro share of 355 MW in 2032. The Metro 440 MW block of 2031 is Mullin Creek 2, which GEM already tracks under Missouri. GEM has no Buchanan Bluffs plant. This is a handoff for the Missouri batch.

monitor.plant_name: Kansas City Board of Public Utilities 237 MW combustion turbine option
monitor.monitor_reason: The Board's 2024 plan studies a 237 MW gas combustion turbine for 2039 only as one case, and the recommended plan builds no gas.
monitor.note: The Kansas City Board of Public Utilities 2024 resource plan was read in full. A saved copy is at https://web.archive.org/web/20250402202525/https://www.bpu.com/Portals/0/pdf/2024-BPU_IRP_Report-2024_11-4-2024.pdf and the live copy is at https://bpu.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2024-BPU_IRP_Report-2024-FINAL.pdf. Study case 2, on page 5-28, retires Nearman Creek 1 at the end of 2038 and adds a 237 MW simple cycle combustion turbine in 2039. Page 6-45 says new conventional thermal generation did not appear appreciably in the results, and recommends that "new and highly efficient natural gas-fired thermal power plants still be included as possible options". So gas stays an option and nothing is committed. The plan gives no site and no filing.

monitor.monitor_reason: Two small replacement gas turbines of about 13.3 MW each are being built at Riverton, far under the 50 MW bar.
monitor.note: Liberty's Empire District Electric asked the Missouri Public Service Commission in case EA-2023-0131 to build two replacement combustion turbines at Riverton, Kansas. The Second Amended Application at https://efis.psc.mo.gov/Document/Display/768252 and the Staff Report of March 8, 2024 at https://efis.psc.mo.gov/Document/Display/773603 give each turbine a nominal net capacity of 13.3 MW, dual fuel, replacing the 1988 Units 10 and 11 of 16.3 MW each, with service expected in July 2026. The EIA-860M table for August 2026 lists Riverton generators 13 and 14 at 13.5 MW each, planned. The Southwest Power Pool list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows GEN-2024-GR4, a 27.14 MW replacement at Riverton 452, commercial operation 5/8/2026, with the interconnection agreement signed. All of that is about 27 MW in total, under the bar. The old units are not in GEM. Check again to see whether the new units start and whether GEM wants units this small at an existing plant. Liberty's separate Missouri request for a 240 to 250 MW combined cycle plant called Stateline is in Missouri.
